source_document.body:
EV Realty has broken ground on a 9 MW electric truck charging site in Torrance, California, that will have 50 charging ports when it opens to commercial fleets in mid-2027.
The company announced the groundbreaking Tuesday. Torrance is its second site in Southern California, after a 76-port hub in San Bernardino opened in April .
The hub is aimed at trucks serving the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, inland distribution centers, and air cargo around Los Angeles International Airport.
California Transportation Commission records show 20 of the 50 ports will use the Megawatt Charging System, or MCS, at up to 1.2 MW. The other 30 will be standard DC fast chargers at up to 350 kW. The site at 18715 S. Western Ave. sits beside Interstate 405 with a direct connection to Interstate 110.
Outpost, which has invested in EV Realty, added the 2.2-acre property to its truck terminal network in March and is a partner on the project along with ParWest and Synop.
Redesign added megawatt chargers
Under the commission’s original scope, the site would have had 60 ports, most rated at up to 300 kW, with 7.6 MW of total capacity. Commission records from March show EV Realty cut the count to 50 ports and raised capacity to 9 MW because the lower-power layout needed more space than the site had. Caltrans, which recommended the change, said the MCS ports would shorten charging times for trucks built to use them.
“With ultra-high-powered MCS charging, a drayage operator operating trucks from this site can run three, maybe even four turns per truck, per day, into the ports,” EV Realty CEO Patrick Sullivan said Tuesday at the groundbreaking. “That means more money and a more sustainable freight economy, with reduced local air impacts, for both the carriers and the shippers.”
The ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach proposed in September paying zero-emission trucks $60 per terminal visit, up to $36,000 a year, under a three-year incentive program. In July, 613 such trucks called at the Port of Long Beach, according to port figures reported by Container News . That was nearly 3.6% of the 16,853 drayage trucks with access to San Pedro Bay terminals.
State grant covers part of the $22.1 million cost
The project’s budget is $22.1 million. A $7.9 million Trade Corridor Enhancement Program grant pays for part of construction, and EV Realty is covering the remaining $14.2 million. The cost rose from $18.37 million with the redesign, and EV Realty agreed to absorb the increase.
Southern California Edison’s fleet charging rebate and a conditional California Energy Commission award also support the project, in amounts the release does not give.
EV Realty buys sites where utility power is already available, an approach FreightWaves detailed in 2024 . The Torrance site has 9.9 MW of grid capacity, according to its state funding agreement.
“By providing access to power when and where it’s needed, we are addressing one of the primary constraints to electrification at scale,” Sullivan said in the release. “Our Powered Properties are ideally located to meet fleet operator needs, and all our sites have ready access to grid power without lengthy utility upgrades.”
An earlier state schedule had construction finishing Feb. 6, 2026. The end date is now June 30, 2027, after permitting delays at two outside agencies, including the city of Torrance.
The release does not name any fleets signed up for the Torrance site. The San Bernardino hub opened with J.B. Hunt, Gate City Beverage, and electric carrier Nevoya as customers.
Second site in a Southern California network
Beyond Torrance, EV Realty has announced future projects in Stockton and Ontario, California. The company said it is on track to have more than 100 MCS ports across Southern California by mid-2027.
“This site will connect with our San Bernardino charging hub, creating the beginning of our network in Southern California,” Chief Commercial Officer Suncheth Bhat said at the groundbreaking. “Being near the ports of LA and Long Beach, we are at the very epicenter of the movement of goods in this country. Few places in the country move more freight than where we are right now, and few places in the country are next door to a King’s Hawaiian, making this soon-to-be the best-smelling truck charging hub in the country.”
Next-generation trucks such as the Tesla Semi will be rolling out at scale when the site opens, the company said. Tesla plans to expand Semi deliveries next year after starting volume production in the third quarter.
“2027 is shaping up to be a year of real growth for this sector as truck technology continues to improve, charging networks expand in key freight hubs, and fleet operators see the potential to save money by going electric,” Bhat said in the release.
Why it matters: Drayage carriers at the San Pedro Bay ports weighing battery-electric trucks will have a shared megawatt-charging site near the terminals by mid-2027. Those buying at least 10 trucks can apply by Dec. 3 for up to $300,000 each from the Port of Los Angeles.
